section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1982
title: MAINING 5 STATES REGISTERED A DECLINE OVER 1981. THE HIGHEST INCREASE IN SUICIDES WAS REGISTERED IN MANIPUR (583 ·3 %) though the numerical increase was of 35 suicide cases only. THE SECOND HIGHEST INCREASE IN SUICIDES WAS REGISTERED IN Bihar (62 ·3 %) followed by Karnataka (34 ·3 %), Punjab (27.7 %), Tripura (26 ·1 %), Orissa (22 ·5 %), Madhya Pradesh (19 ·9 %), Maharashtra (19 ·3 %), Meghalaya (16 ·2 %), Jammu & Kashmir (15.8 %), Tamil Nadu (13.5 %), Kerala (12 ·6 %), Rajasthan (11 ·7), Gujrat (10 ·4), Himachal Pradesh (5 ·9), West Bengal (5 ·2 %) and Andhra Pradesh (2 ·6 %). THE 5 STATES TO REGISTER A DECLINE OVER NAGALAND (58 ·3 %), HARYANA (23 ·2 %), U. P. (19 ·5 %), Sikkim (19 ·1 %), AND ASSAM (10 ·9 %). ALL THE UNION TERRITORIES TAKEN TOGETHER REGISTERED AN INCREASE OF 24 ·1 % IN THE TOTAL NUMBER OF SUICIDES DURING 1982 OVER 1981. OUT OF 9 UTS, FIVE UTS REGISTERED AN INCREASE IN THE TOTAL NUMBER OF SUICIDES DURING 1982 OVER 1981 AND THE FIVE UTS TO REGISTER THIS INCREASE WERE A&N ISLANDS (84 ·6 %), PONDICHERRY (56 ·4 %), Chandigarh (23 ·5 %), ARUNACHAL PRADESH (15 ·0 %) AND DELHI (9 ·6 %). MIZORAM AND D&N HAVELI REGISTERED A DECLINE OF 50 ·0 PERCENT AND 6 ·3 PERCENT RESPECTIVELY, WHILE GOA, DAMAN & DIU AND LAKSHADweep did not register any change in the number of SUICIDES in comparison to previous year. OUT OF 12 METROPOLITAN CITIES CORRECT DATA FROM LUCKNOW CITY WAS NOT AVAILABLE AND THE FIGURES OF 11 REMAINING CITIES TAKEN TOGETHER REGISTERED AN INCREASE OF 1 ·7 PERCENT DURING 1982 OVER 1981. ONLY TWO CITIES VIZ., MADRASAND KANPUR REGISTERED A DECLINE OF 33 ·6 % AND 12 ·0 % RESPECTIVELY WHILE 9 CITIES REGISTERED AN INCREASE THE HIGHEST INCREASE BEING REGISTERED IN CALCUTTA (64 ·0 %) AND THE LOWEST IN BOMBAY (2 ·9 %). notes: Distribution of Suicides according to Age

The statistics of suicides by age revealed that the maximum suicides (19,917) were committed by persons belonging to the age group of 18-30 years i.e., 44.6% of the total suicides reported in the country and the minimum (5,574) were committed by the persons above 50 years of age sharing 12.4 per cent of the total suicides in the country. The total number of suicides committed by the persons between 30 to 50 years of age was (13,137) which registered 29.4 per cent of total suicides in India while the persons below 18 years of age accounted for 13.6 per cent of the total suicides reported during 1982 registering a total number of 6,104 suicide cases. The age-wise distribution of suicides for all the States together and the country as a whole was almost the same during 1982 and it was almost the same for the Union Territories and the Metropolitan cities as a whole.
